stories.title: MEASURED: 73ms per engine spawn x 676 run() call sites = ~49s of pure node startup, in ONE file, on 16 cores. node parallelizes across FILES only (proven: 4 files x 3s = 3.3s wall).

keep the :996 self-heal test repo-less (it is the only coverage of the unverifiable branch and it caught the two-state guard bug); rename it to say so and ADD a git-repo twin for the verified path
audit every doesNotMatch/empty-string assertion in the suite for the same vacuous-pass shape, not just the ones added for gh#65

MEASURED RESULT: 118s serial -> ~46s parallel (2.6x) across 11 files. 18 files was WORSE (46s) than 11 -- runner startup overhead. Floor is the slowest file (21s); the 46-21 gap is tmpdir/spawn contention, not concurrency (--test-concurrency=16 changed nothing).

GLOB LANDMINE: node --test scripts/test (a DIRECTORY) does not work on Node 26 -- it treats the arg as a module, dies MODULE_NOT_FOUND, reports '1 test'. Only the shell glob works. Documented in the hook so nobody 'simplifies' it.

MUTATION-TESTED the guard tests: disabling the guard initially left 4 of 5 still PASSING, because gitRepo()'s baseline commit touches 4 files and looksLikeUnloggedMinimalDetour rejects >3 -- they were passing on the file-count rule, not the guard. REMAINING (low): 3 doesNotMatch(parseBrief(...)) can be vacuous since parseBrief returns '' on empty brief output.

epics.description: Evidence from operations-ship-their-inverses (0.46.0). The change adopted a practice its task list never asked for: after shipping drop-detour, every guard it added was NEUTERED in turn and the suite re-run, with the whole batch saved as red-3.5-mutation-evidence.txt in the change directory. Six mutants; five died; ONE SURVIVED AND WAS A REAL DEFECT — removing drop-detour's own reconcileNeeded recompute left all 17 tests green, because render() runs after the save and the drift heal cleared the flag one write later, which is exactly the intermediate state gate-integrity says the engine cannot produce. Every assertion read the final value, so nothing could tell the two mechanisms apart. The fix was to assert on the drop's OWN stderr. Nothing in the seven required task items would have found it: item 1 enumerates call sites and inverses of the thing being guarded, item 2 verifies the commit, and both gates read a diff. A test that cannot go red is invisible to all of them. Proposal: a numbered required task item — 'prove every guard this change adds can fail' — carrying the batch form (mutate, run, record, restore), the artifact convention (a named file in the change directory, so the gate can read it rather than trust a sentence), and the rule that a SURVIVING mutant is a finding to be explained, not a redundant test to delete. Precedent for the form: docs/lessons/a-guard-can-check-the-wrong-half already states the habit and has no mechanism; measured here, the habit found a defect the whole gate stack missed.

epics.description: FRICTION ROUTED BY functional-assertion-test-split (0.47.0), required task item 7. File with /pm:feedback as well. EVIDENCE: runHookAgainstFixture (scripts/test/fixtures/helpers.mjs) builds a scratch git repository, copies the REAL .githooks/pre-commit into it, and runs it -- deliberately, so the hook is exercised rather than a stub. 6.4 added a step to that hook (the drift script), and the three fixtures that run it went red for a reason that had nothing to do with what they test: the fixture held a hook but not the script, and the script but not the minimum tree it reads (scripts/lib/, conductor.mjs, the two bucket directories). The fix was to have the fixture construct that skeleton -- which means every future hook step has to be mirrored into a fixture builder, and nothing enforces the mirror. Measured cost: half an hour of diagnosis for a one-line hook insertion, and the failure mode is the worst kind -- three unrelated tests red, all pointing at the hook rather than at themselves. Candidate fix: derive the fixture tree from the hook's own invocations, or give the hook a single well-known entry point so a fixture can stub it by contract.

crossSpecReview.reviewer: INLINE review by the applying agent, NOT fresh-context lenses — this run's discipline forbids subagent dispatch, and that limitation is recorded here rather than papered over. Six questions over the release's two spec files (engine-invocation, suite-certification): (1) contradiction — none; the near-miss (one-process assertion half vs two-independent-invocations) is mutual dependency, not conflict. (2) double ownership — none; conductor.mjs's covers referencing the conformance set is a reference, and engine-invocation explicitly declines to restate verb-surface's refusal classes. (3) unmeetable — none in the specs. (4) gaps against proposal What-Changes — one: ci.yml's non-descending syntax loop has no requirement; declined as POLISH. (5) vocabulary forks — two, change-internal: "double" vs "fake", "change-triggered bucket" vs "sweeps bucket"; declined, renaming churns a passed Gate 1 contract for no behaviour change. (6) shared chokepoint — the single-process assertion half with injected streams is load-bearing for BOTH specs; guarded on each side (1.2 exits, 3.5 roots, 5.2 spawns). FINDING raised against the TASK LIST, not the specs: git.mjs's resolvedCommitCache is keyed by VALUE ONLY (unreachedCache by head+commits), so two invocations in one process against two roots share it and a hex abbreviation resolving in one repository and not the other gets the first repository's answer — engine-invocation forbids observing another invocation's values, and no task keys those caches; handled in the gateway work (4.2) rather than by amending a spec that is already correct. Verdict pass: no BLOCK found in either spec file; one BLOCK-level finding against tasks.md, acted on. 2026-09-20

crossSpecReview.reviewer: inline foreground cross-spec review of the 0.48.0 spec set — no fresh-context subagents were available in this run, so the reviewer is the applying agent, which read both of this change's deltas in full and answered the six questions. NOTE ON THE ENUMERATED SET: the engine enumerated FOUR specs, not two — the extra pair is functional-assertion-test-split/specs/{suite-certification,engine-invocation}/spec.md, the stale LIVE duplicate of the tree ab171b7 archived (task 0.4), which the release-scope enumeration reaches because the live directory was copied rather than moved. Those two are byte-identical to the archived originals and are the same two capabilities this change deltas, so the review covers them; the duplicate is filed separately under 0.4 rather than repaired here. BLOCKS (fixed in this commit): engine-invocation's 'the invocation that used the in-memory store created no file' scenario was unreachable — init() writes CLAUDE.md (rules.mjs:1097) and .gitignore through raw fs, both deliberately outside the store per design D1, so the scenario was narrowed to the store's own footprint and an explicit boundary paragraph was added. CONTRADICTION: none. suite-certification's rungs and engine-invocation's per-call store agree; 'both rungs run in one invocation of one process' does not collide with 'two invocations in one process are independent' — different claims about different things, and no scenario still speaks of the assertion half as one on-disk directory (the modified requirement and all four of its scenarios name the rungs). DOUBLE OWNERSHIP: none. engine-invocation owns the caller's contract and now states the store's boundary; suite-certification owns rung membership and names the store only as the mechanism a unit test obtains a value through, which is the split task 0.2 asked for. UNMEETABLE: the one above, now fixed. GAPS against the proposal's What Changes: none found — the three artifacts I1 added (session-claim.json, commit-observe.json + .lock, write-conflicts.log.prev) and render's three reads (projectMd pre-image render.mjs:306, the stamp's mtime test :356, detoursLog :276) are each carried by a task (1.2, 1.3). VOCABULARY: consistent within the spec set; POLISH declined — the file rung's directory is still named assert/ (the half's own name) while the unit rung's is unit/, so the rungs are named on disk as required but the names are not parallel; renaming is out of this change's scope. CHOKEPOINTS: homeOf() (certification.mjs:63) and the two-glob runner invocation the hook and ci.yml both hand to one runner are each owned by exactly one capability. Recorded AFTER the amendment above, so the recorded hashes cover the amended text.
